solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Polish local back on the game

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: RU is rugby union, often just 'the game' to its fans

indicators.note: back means the word for local is read from its end

parts.note: a local is a British pub, the one nearest your home

explanation.surface: A pub regular tells you the match has resumed back at their local.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is a British drinker's nearest pub, and 'the game' is rugby union to its fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub up silver or brass is to give it a shine, a verb synonym of polish.

clue.text: Show over, gather before Conference

indicators.note: the gathering word comes before the Conference one

parts.note: to reap a crop is to gather it
Conference is a popular British variety of pear

explanation.surface: A show is over, and the delegates gather before the conference.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a common pear variety in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up again, appearing over again, is what something does when it returns to view.

clue.text: English girl's last but one composition for jazz interval

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are arranged afresh
the last letter of girl's word is taken, before its possessive ending

explanation.surface: An English girl's penultimate composition is for a jazz interlude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl' supplies its final letter; 'composition' rearranges that letter and 'but one', and English adds the closing letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue note is a flattened third or seventh in jazz and blues, a musical interval.

clue.text: Get satirists performing curse

parts.note: to get or put something somewhere are near synonyms
satirists mock, so they are the mockers
a show that is on is being performed

explanation.surface: Bring the satirists on stage to curse.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the mockers on something is British slang for jinxing it, bringing bad luck upon it.

clue.text: Start making an impression having landed work on ship

parts.note: to have landed something is to have got it
OP is short for opus, a musical work
RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Having docked, a sailor gets to work on board a ship and starts to make an impression.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers and books start being printed, physically making an impression on paper, when they go to the printing stage.

clue.text: Carriage entrance is for picking up only

indicators.note: picking up means catching a sound by ear, so only the sound matters

parts.note: a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: A sign at an entrance says it is for collecting passengers only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picking up' is ear-pickup, the homophone signal: GATE and GAIT sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage means the way one holds and moves one's body, which is one's walking manner.

clue.text: Parts of China party?

definitions.meaning: fractions, each one of twenty equal portions
the celebration of the anniversary marked with china, the twentieth wedding anniversary

explanation.surface: Sections of the Chinese party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China party' suggests the Communist Party, but china is the traditional gift for a twentieth wedding anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole cut into twenty equal fractions gives these portions, and the china anniversary comes after twenty years of marriage.

clue.text: Happy choirboys ultimately leading fabulous, special sort of life

indicators.note: fabulous suggests something fantastic or invented, so the letters are reworked
ultimately takes the final letter of leading

explanation.surface: Cheerful choristers end up heading a wonderful, special life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives G, which joins HAPPYCHOIRBOYS for 'fabulous' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychobiography is a life story that focuses on its subject's psychology, a specialised kind of biography.

clue.text: Race Elizabeth and Nicholas are holding together

indicators.note: the two names each hold a run of letters, and those runs are joined together into one word

parts.note: the name Elizabeth ends in these three letters, the run it holds
Nic is a short form of Nicholas, its opening letters

explanation.surface: A couple named Elizabeth and Nicholas are clinging together.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of ElizabETH and the start of NICholas are joined, skipping the link word between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnic relates to a people sharing descent or culture, the sense of race in this adjective.

clue.text: Son, having drawn on pot, gets fired

parts.note: toked means drew on a cannabis joint, pot being cannabis

explanation.surface: A son caught smoking cannabis gets sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoked means fuelled, as of a fire or boiler, so it is a synonym of fired in that sense.

clue.text: Motorists about to leave home finally choose somewhere in France

indicators.note: the motorists' letters go about, i.e. around, the verb for leaving

parts.note: the AA is Britain's Automobile Association, a motoring organisation
to quit is to leave
in means at home

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of choose

explanation.surface: Drivers about to set off from home pick a destination in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the British motoring organisation; motorists here are its members.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquitaine is a region in the south-west of France, so it is an example of a French place.

clue.text: Brute rounds on pretentious toff

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it comes after it

parts.note: a yah is a braying upper-class British type, from their way of saying yes
two round shapes look like the letters O and O

explanation.surface: A thuggish type goes after a snobbish upper-class twit.
explanation.definitionFit: In Gulliver's Travels the Yahoos are brutish humanoids, and the word now means any coarse, savage person.

clue.text: Cutting insignificant church visits

indicators.note: the church abbreviation goes into, i.e. visits, the word for insignificant

parts.note: puny means feeble or insignificant

explanation.surface: A minor church gets a visit, perhaps for a ribbon-cutting ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting remark is sharp and forceful, and punchy describes writing or comments with that bite.

clue.text: Parasite from horse burrowing into poor titmice

indicators.note: the horse letter digs inside the scrambled birds, as a burrowing pest would
poor suggests the birds are in bad shape, so their letters are reordered

parts.note: H is slang for heroin, known as horse, and an abbreviation used in crosswords

explanation.surface: A parasite passes from a horse into some unfortunate small birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges TITMICE into ITCMITE, and 'burrowing into' puts H inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The itch mite is the tiny arachnid that burrows into skin and causes scabies, a parasite.

clue.text: A number one turn, time and time again

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a go is a turn
musical time is rhythm

explanation.surface: First, take a turn, time after time.
explanation.definitionFit: I Got Rhythm is a Gershwin song, and a song is a musical number.

clue.text: Song bird relies on following it around

indicators.note: the bird and relies on pieces come after, i.e. follow, the reversed it
around means the two letters for it are turned round

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is 'it' in old slang
bird is British slang for time in prison
to go by a rule is to rely on it

explanation.surface: A bird depends on following something round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving time in jail, and 'it' is old slang for sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: As Time Goes By is the famous song played by Sam in the film Casablanca.

clue.text: Popular pro

explanation.definitionFit: Being well thought of is being in someone's good books, and backing a motion is being on its side.

clue.text: Artwork from film projecting feature on grammar school

indicators.note: in a down clue, the film and feature sit on top of the school letters

parts.note: ET is Spielberg's film
the chin is a protruding facial feature

explanation.surface: An art piece from a film shows a feature in a grammar school.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from metal plates incised with acid, a form of artwork.

clue.text: Put the lid on canopy over engine that's growing hot

parts.note: to scotch a rumour is to put the lid on it, stopping it
the bonnet is the British word for a car's hood

explanation.surface: Someone closes up the cover over an engine that is overheating.
explanation.walkthrough: A car's bonnet is what Americans call the hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scotch bonnet is a fiercely pungent chilli pepper, a cultivated plant whose fruit burns the mouth.

clue.text: No pained reactions arise after a fainting

indicators.note: the turned letters come after the A
arise in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: ows are cries of pain

explanation.surface: No cries of pain occur after someone faints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arise' turns NOOWS into SWOON, which comes after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a swoon is being in a faint, an old-fashioned adverb or adjective for passing out.

clue.text: Judge a pain in the neck mostly about immigrant's case

indicators.note: the shortened pain goes around the case letters
mostly drops the final letter

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: A judge is a real nuisance over an immigrant's legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the neck pain; 'case' picks immigrant's outer letters, which go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic is someone who judges or evaluates the quality of something, and judge can mean that as a noun.

clue.text: Raucous Indian in school yard

indicators.note: the Indian goes in the school abbreviation

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A rowdy Indian pupil is out in the school yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Something screechy makes harsh, high cries, which is a raucous noise.

clue.text: An inspired suggestion?

definitions.meaning: something inhaled, taken into the lungs, is literally inspired air
a slight hint, as in 'a whisper of scandal'

explanation.surface: Someone offers a brilliant idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspired' reads as brilliant, but here it means breathed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Air drawn in is inspired, and a mere trace or hint of something is also called this, as in a whiff of scandal.

clue.text: The cheapest promotion for this tablet?

parts.note: a one-penny item is about the cheapest, 1P looking like IP
an ad promotes something

explanation.surface: A bargain-basement advertising campaign for a tablet.
explanation.walkthrough: The penny is the smallest British coin, written 1p, which looks like IP.
explanation.definitionFit: The iPad is Apple's tablet computer, an example of the device.

clue.text: Nothing put forward in musketeer's pledges

indicators.note: the zero letter is moved to the front within the name

parts.note: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A musketeer's sworn vows contain nothing new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put forward in' moves the O of ATHOS to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaths are solemn promises sworn before witnesses, so they are pledges.

clue.text: Leading in platoon, prepared for further advance

indicators.note: prepared signals the letters are got ready anew, i.e. rearranged

parts.note: a team that is up is leading

explanation.surface: The man out front of a platoon is ready to move further forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only places the leading word among the platoon's letters; 'prepared' then rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up loan is extra borrowing added to an existing loan, an additional advance of money.

clue.text: Given handle, stir, with pole, a lot of water

parts.note: stir and nick are both British slang for prison
N is the North Pole
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone takes hold of a handle to stir, using a pole in a lot of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name, so to be given one is to be named informally.

clue.text: Scene of action initially settled on years before

indicators.note: in an across clue, the settled letter goes on, i.e. after, the others

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of settled

explanation.surface: A battlefield is first settled on, years in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres in Belgium was the site of several major First World War battles, a place of military action.
